what: Elevance Health is one of the largest US health insurers, operating Blue Cross Blue Shield plans in 14 states. It also runs Carelon, which provides pharmacy benefits and care services to its own members and to others.
customers: Employers buying group coverage, individuals on exchange plans, and Medicare and Medicaid members.
money: commercial, Medicare Advantage and Medicaid insurance premiums
pharmacy benefits, behavioural health and care management services
moat: Exclusive Blue Cross Blue Shield licences in its states, which give it the largest provider networks and the lowest negotiated prices there.
risks: Medicaid members who stayed on after the pandemic turned out to be sicker and costlier than expected
Medical costs have risen faster than premiums across the industry
Government decides Medicare and Medicaid payment rates
Profit margins are thin: about three cents on each revenue dollar
opportunities: Premiums are being repriced upward as contracts renew, which usually restores margins over about two years
Carelon lets it keep services profit that would otherwise go to outside vendors
The shares trade at a low multiple of earnings compared with their own history
watch: The benefit expense ratio, which shows the share of premiums paid out in claims.
